title: LLM Inference Serving
subtitle: Schedule prefill, decode and KV memory across GPU replicas with explicit overload and recovery contracts.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Request shape and targets
practice_prompts.hint: Which token, latency and failure questions change the design? State the assumptions you would use.

practice_prompts.label: Size compute, slots and KV
practice_prompts.hint: Derive replica-seconds, Little's Law concurrency and per-sequence KV, then say which binds.

practice_prompts.label: Admit, route and batch
practice_prompts.hint: Trace one request through admission, power-of-two routing and continuous batching with chunked prefill.

practice_prompts.label: Failure, overload and cost
practice_prompts.hint: Kill a GPU before and after the first token, overload a tenant, then answer the GPU-bill pivot.

rubric: Asks for input and output token distributions before sizing, and names prefill, decode and KV as the three capacity facts.
Prices a request in replica-seconds (0.15 for the anchor), cross-checks slots with Little's Law and states which constraint binds.
Explains why continuous batching beats static batching for variable output and what chunked prefill trades.
Routes by free KV with power-of-two choices and a replica-side final check, not round-robin.
Distinguishes recovery before and after the first streamed token, with a retry budget and request-ID dedupe.
Bounds admission by tenant tokens, returns 429 early and reports goodput, TTFT, TPOT and queue wait separately.

editorial_review.evidence: 16 November 2026: read all 49 captured sections of source.json against the earlier teach-mode draft paragraph by paragraph. The draft kept every source table but had dropped or flattened specific items: the mid-stream-failure discovery question, the weak/strong answer and spoken line, the A100 caveat, 'say both checks aloud', LLM-versus-code ownership, the three architecture boundaries, gateway input cap, perceived-versus-total streaming latency, the 990 idle steps, queue length as tie-breaker, the Little's Law queue bound, the 64-caller crash, 'latency = wait + queue + 200 ms', review delivery advice, the frozen-screen rule, the 45-minute table (misstated last slot), both verbatim two-minute answers, the 60-second close, reference claims and tokens-after-disconnect. All restored. Structural changes: added walkthrough step 5 (tokenise at the edge, stream and cancel) and step 9 (evaluation), split the junior review from latency diagnosis, gave the five figures specific captions from their actual SVG labels, explained each batching strategy separately with one traced pair, added worked 100K-row arithmetic, corrected Check-yourself answer 8 to the source, and added two labelled drills. The brief keeps a traced request and a related-prompts table; old navigation sections are consolidated, not shown. Uncaptured internal source notes are disclosed in References. Source-problem sweep (2026-11-16): no real source inconsistencies in this case; the only source-pointing aside (the source 'rounds' 214.3 to about 214) was reworded neutrally, keeping both 214 and the 215 strict ceiling.
